Cape Canaveral SLC-37B, 2018-08-12. Parker Solar Probe required one of the highest launch energies ever flown (C3 ≈ 154 km²/s²; only New Horizons' was higher) to break out of Earth's orbital motion enough to fall into a Sun-grazing trajectory. The third-stage Star 48BV solid motor was a custom addition to the Delta IV Heavy stack.
Delta IV Heavy + Star 48BV stack delivers Parker onto a Venus-encounter trajectory.
2018-10-03. First of seven Venus encounters that progressively lower perihelion. Each VGA bleeds orbital energy; perihelion shrinks ~3 R☉ per encounter.
2018-11-05. First close approach to the Sun: 0.16 AU (35 R☉). Parker became the closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown, beating Helios 2's 1976 record.
2021-02-20. Fourth VGA tightens perihelion further toward the 9.86 R☉ target.
2021-04-28. Perihelion 8 dipped below the Alfvén critical surface — the formal boundary of the Sun's corona. Parker became the first spacecraft to enter the Sun's atmosphere.
2023-08-21. Sixth VGA prepares the final two record-setting perihelia.

2024-12-24. Christmas Eve eve. Parker reached 6.1 M km from the Sun's surface (~9.86 R☉, 0.046 AU) — the closest any spacecraft has ever been to the Sun. Speed at perihelion: ~191 km/s, the fastest human-made object ever. The heat shield's solar-facing surface reached ~1,377 °C; the spacecraft bus behind it remained at room temperature. Its beacon confirmed a safe pass on 26 December 2024.
Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown (6.1 M km, 9.86 R☉); first spacecraft to enter the solar corona (2021-04-28); fastest human-made object (~191 km/s)

Parker Solar Probe ran one of the highest-energy launches ever flown — C3 of 154 km²/s² (only New Horizons' was higher), requiring a custom Star 48BV solid third stage atop a Delta IV Heavy just to escape Earth into a Sun-falling trajectory. Seven Venus gravity assists over six years progressively lowered perihelion from 0.16 AU (P1, 2018-11-05) to 0.046 AU (P22, 2024-12-24 — 9.86 solar radii, 6.1 million km from the surface). At P8 in 2021-04-28 Parker dipped below the Alfvén critical surface — the first spacecraft ever to enter the Sun's corona. At P22 it reached ~191 km/s, becoming the fastest human-made object ever. The 11.43-cm carbon-carbon heat shield sustained 1,377 °C while the spacecraft bus 1 metre behind it remained at room temperature.
